result.summary: Our patch adds a canonicalize-then-verify-inside-base check (isPathUnderBase) invoked in both ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource and ExternalResourceHandler.getResource, for both the primary path and the welcome-file sub-case, returning null when the resolved path escapes the configured base. This is the CWE-022 defense-of-record and, for external resources, is actually stronger than the official fix (it resolves symlinks via getCanonicalPath and avoids the sibling-prefix false-accept of the official string startsWith). It is applied at the same detection points as the official fix (the two resource handlers); it omits only the official's non-security plumbing (StaticFilesFolder tracking, warn-logging wrapper), achieving the equivalent "not served" outcome by returning null. The class appears closed at the sink.
result.root_cause: Untrusted request path is combined with the static-files base and resolved to a File without verifying the canonicalized result stays inside the configured base directory, allowing "../" traversal to escape the static root.

dimensions.rationale: Boundary re-check at the filesystem sink neutralizes the whole traversal class, not just one payload; canonicalization normalizes .. and separators before the resource is built.
dimensions.evidence: AbstractResourceHandler.isPathUnderBase uses File.getCanonicalPath() + startsWith(base+separator); called in ClassPathResourceHandler/ExternalResourceHandler getResource before resource creation and return null on escape.
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Guards the actual filesystem/trust boundary in both handlers where the tainted path becomes a File, not a caller symptom.
dimensions.evidence: isPathUnderBase(baseResource, addedPath) inserted immediately after addPaths() and before new ClassPathResource/new ExternalResource.
dimensions.label: Root cause vs symptom

dimensions.rationale: Both handlers plus the welcome-file sub-path are covered, matching the official detection points; slight residual uncertainty whether a separate JAR resolution path bypasses ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource.
dimensions.evidence: welcomePath re-checked via isPathUnderBase in both handlers; official-only StaticFilesConfiguration consume-wrapper not replicated (compensated by returning null).
dimensions.label: Completeness / variants

dimensions.rationale: Same defensive strategy (verify resolved path stays under configured base) and same location; different, stronger mechanism (canonicalization vs configured-folder string match).
dimensions.evidence: Official uses DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainst* with removeLeadingAndTrailingSlashesFrom(path).startsWith(StaticFilesFolder.local()); ours uses getCanonicalPath prefix check in the same getResource methods.
dimensions.label: Developer-intent alignment

dimensions.rationale: Legitimate under-base paths still pass (consistent fake-root normalization for classpath, real canonicalization for external); added unit tests pass, but no regression suite was executed to confirm.
dimensions.evidence: withLeadingSlash normalizes both operands; regressions_ran:0 / regressions_passed:null in execution results is a weak signal.
dimensions.label: Functional correctness

dimensions.rationale: Safe standard primitive; IOException from getCanonicalPath is swallowed by the surrounding catch(Exception) → returns null (fail-closed). Minor inherent TOCTOU between canonical check and later file open.
dimensions.evidence: isPathUnderBase throws IOException, called inside getResource's existing try/catch(Exception e); no regex/shell introduced.
dimensions.label: No new defects

dimensions.rationale: Tight, localized: one shared helper in the abstract base plus two-line guards in each handler.
dimensions.evidence: AbstractResourceHandler.isPathUnderBase/withLeadingSlash + minimal insertions in ClassPathResourceHandler and ExternalResourceHandler.
dimensions.label: Minimality

dimensions.rationale: Canonicalize-to-real-path then verify containment is the CWE-022 defense-of-record; for external resources it resolves symlinks and avoids the official's sibling-prefix false-accept.
dimensions.evidence: candidate.equals(base) || candidate.startsWith(base + File.separator) over getCanonicalPath results.
dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: No regression suite was executed (regressions_ran:0, regressions_passed:null) and pov_before_reproduced was false, so verification of both closure and non-regression rests on code analysis rather than execution evidence.

Does not replicate the official StaticFilesConfiguration.consume warn-logging wrapper; blocked traversals are silently returned as null (functionally safe but no audit log). Also omits StaticFilesFolder tracking used by the official fix.
Coverage of any JAR-served resolution path that does not route through ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource is unverified from the provided context.
